source.text: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες· Τίς ἄρα μείζων ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν;

records.literal_gloss: In that the hour came the disciples to the Jesus saying, Who then greater is in the kingdom of the heavens?

en.L: At that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, "Who then is greatest in the kingdom of the heavens?"
en.B: Just then the disciples came to Jesus with a question: "So who ranks highest in the kingdom of heaven?"
en.R: At that time the followers came to Jesus and asked, "Who is the most important person in the kingdom of heaven?"

es.L: En aquella hora se acercaron los discípulos a Jesús, diciendo: «¿Quién es, pues, el mayor en el reino de los cielos?».
es.B: En ese momento los discípulos se acercaron a Jesús con una pregunta: «Entonces, ¿quién ocupa el lugar más alto en el reino de los cielos?».
es.R: En ese tiempo los discípulos se acercaron a Jesús y le preguntaron: «¿Quién es la persona más importante en el reino de los cielos?».

fr.L: À cette heure-là, les disciples s’approchèrent de Jésus en disant : « Qui donc est le plus grand dans le royaume des cieux ? »
fr.B: À ce moment-là, les disciples vinrent trouver Jésus avec une question : « Qui donc a le rang le plus élevé dans le royaume des cieux ? »
fr.R: À ce moment-là, les disciples sont venus voir Jésus. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Qui est le plus important dans le royaume des cieux ? »

sw.L: Wakati huo huo wanafunzi walimkaribia Yesu, wakisema, "Basi, ni nani mkubwa zaidi katika ufalme wa mbinguni?"
sw.B: Wakati huo wanafunzi walimjia Yesu na swali: "Basi ni nani aliye na cheo cha juu kabisa katika ufalme wa mbinguni?"
sw.R: Wakati huo wanafunzi walimjia Yesu, wakamwuliza, "Ni nani aliye muhimu kuliko wote katika ufalme wa mbinguni?"

vi.L: Vào giờ ấy, các môn đồ đến gần Đức Giê-xu và nói: "Vậy thì ai là lớn hơn cả trong vương quốc thiên đàng?"
vi.B: Lúc ấy, các môn đồ đến hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Vậy ai là người lớn nhất trong vương quốc thiên đàng?"
vi.R: Lúc ấy, các môn đồ đến hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Trong vương quốc thiên đàng, ai là người quan trọng nhất?"

ko.L: 그때에 제자들이 예수께 나아와 말했다. "그러면 천국에서는 누가 더 큽니까?"
ko.B: 바로 그때에 제자들이 예수께 와서 물었다. "그러면 천국에서는 누가 가장 큰 사람입니까?"
ko.R: 그때 제자들이 예수께 와서 여쭈었다. "천국에서는 누가 가장 높은 사람입니까?"

decisions.choice: at that hour: the question follows the talk of the temple tax (17:24-27)
decisions.reason: Matthew joins the scenes closely. Jesus has just spoken of the sons of the king as free; the disciples now ask about rank in the kingdom.

decisions.choice: greater: the comparative form used for "greatest"
decisions.reason: The Greek of the time often used the comparative where a superlative is meant. The disciples ask who will rank first (compare 20:20-28).

decisions.choice: then: so, in that case, drawing on what has gone before
decisions.reason: The small word marks the question as following from something already said, perhaps Peter's place in 16:18-19 and 17:1. It does not mark time.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of the heavens (L); the kingdom of heaven (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 3:2, Literal keeps the plural and Balanced and Readable use the familiar form.

decisions.choice: the most important person
decisions.reason: Readable says what "greatest" means here: the one with the highest rank.

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos
decisions.reason: Matthew's name for God's kingdom, said the same way at every level throughout the book and recorded once in this passage. The Spanish plural "los cielos" is natural in this phrase, as the Greek plural is.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Jesus's speech in its own tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As in Mark and Luke: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers meet stories, so Readable uses it. The chapter is mostly speech (18:3-20, 18:22-35), which keeps the tenses of speech, the parable of 18:23-34 included.

decisions.choice: le royaume des cieux at every level; les disciples at Readable too
decisions.reason: The term settled for the New Testament: the French plural "des cieux" is the familiar form and also keeps the Greek plural, so all three levels can share it. English Readable says "followers"; French "disciple" is an everyday word and Mark and Luke keep it at Readable.

decisions.choice: ufalme wa mbinguni
decisions.reason: Matthew's name for God's kingdom, said the same way at every level throughout the book and recorded once in this passage. "Mbinguni" (in heaven) is the natural Swahili form and covers the Greek plural "heavens".

decisions.choice: "vương quốc thiên đàng" at every level
decisions.reason: As settled for Matthew (3:1, 10:7): one phrase at every level, the same words the Vietnamese Matthew uses throughout.

decisions.choice: "lớn hơn cả" (L); "người lớn nhất" (B); "người quan trọng nhất" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek comparative is used for the superlative; Literal keeps a trace of the comparative with "hơn cả", Balanced uses the plain superlative, Readable says what "great" means here, as in Mark 9:34.

decisions.choice: "천국" at every level; "더 큰" (L), "가장 큰 사람" (B), "가장 높은 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: "천국" is the settled Korean Matthew word for "the kingdom of the heavens" at every level. The Greek comparative is used for "greatest" (meaning decision); Literal keeps the comparative, as the Korean Mark 9:34 does, and Readable says "highest" as Mark's Readable does.

decisions.choice: The disciples speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 ("큽니까", "사람입니까")
decisions.reason: People speaking to Jesus use 합쇼체 (style guide, section 4).

source.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ στραφῆτε καὶ γένησθε ὡς τὰ παιδία, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And having called a child he set it in midst of them \v 3 and said, Truly I say to you, if not you turn and become as the children, not not you will enter into the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: And calling a child to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set it in [the] middle of them \v 3 and said, "Truly I tell you, unless you turn and become like the children, you will never enter the kingdom of the heavens.
en.B: He called a little child over and stood the child among them. \v 3 Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Truly I tell you, if you do not turn around and become like children, you will not get into the kingdom of heaven at all.
en.R: Jesus called a little child to come over to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He had the child stand among them. \v 3 Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I tell you the truth, you must change and become like little children. If you do not, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

es.L: Y habiendo llamado a un niñito, lo colocó en medio de ellos \v 3 y dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: si no {{plural_you:se vuelven|os volvéis}} y {{plural_you:llegan|llegáis}} a ser como los niños, de ningún modo {{plural_you:entrarán|entraréis}} en el reino de los cielos.
es.B: Él llamó a un niño pequeño y lo puso de pie en medio de ellos. \v 3 Entonces dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que si no {{plural_you:cambian|cambiáis}} de rumbo y {{plural_you:se hacen|os hacéis}} como niños, no {{plural_you:entrarán|entraréis}} en absoluto en el reino de los cielos.
es.R: Jesús llamó a un niño pequeño para que se acercara a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Hizo que el niño se pusiera de pie en medio de ellos. \v 3 Entonces dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que cambiar y {{plural_you:hacerse|haceros}} como niños pequeños. Si no lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, nunca {{plural_you:entrarán|entraréis}} en el reino de los cielos.

fr.L: Et ayant appelé un enfant [auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le plaça au milieu d’eux \v 3 et dit : « En vérité, je vous le dis, si vous ne changez pas et ne devenez pas comme les enfants, vous n’entrerez jamais dans le royaume des cieux.
fr.B: Il fit venir un petit enfant et le plaça au milieu d’eux. \v 3 Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « En vérité, je vous le dis, si vous ne changez pas de direction pour devenir comme les enfants, vous n’entrerez pas du tout dans le royaume des cieux.
fr.R: Jésus a appelé un petit enfant pour qu’il vienne près de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il l’a fait se tenir au milieu d’eux. \v 3 Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : « Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : vous devez changer et devenir comme de petits enfants. Sinon, vous n’entrerez jamais dans le royaume des cieux.

sw.L: Na akimwita mtoto mdogo [{{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}], akamsimamisha katikati yao \v 3 na kusema, "Kweli nawaambia, msipogeuka na kuwa kama watoto, hakika hamtaingia katika ufalme wa mbinguni.
sw.B: Alimwita mtoto mdogo, akamsimamisha katikati yao. \v 3 Kisha akasema, "Kweli nawaambia, msipogeuka na kuwa kama watoto, hamtaingia kamwe katika ufalme wa mbinguni.
sw.R: Yesu alimwita mtoto mdogo aje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Akamsimamisha katikati yao. \v 3 Kisha akasema, "Nawaambia ukweli, ni lazima mbadilike na kuwa kama watoto wadogo. Msipofanya hivyo, hamtaingia kamwe katika ufalme wa mbinguni.

vi.L: Và gọi một đứa trẻ đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt nó đứng giữa họ \v 3 và nói: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, nếu các con không quay lại và trở nên như những đứa trẻ, các con nhất định sẽ không vào vương quốc thiên đàng.
vi.B: Ngài gọi một em nhỏ đến và cho em đứng giữa họ. \v 3 Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, nếu các con không đổi hướng mà trở nên như các em nhỏ, thì các con chắc chắn không bao giờ được vào vương quốc thiên đàng.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu gọi một em nhỏ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài cho em đứng giữa các môn đồ. \v 3 Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Ta nói thật với các con, các con phải thay đổi và trở nên giống như các em nhỏ. Nếu không, các con sẽ không bao giờ được vào vương quốc thiên đàng.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 어린아이 하나를 [가까이] 불러 그들 가운데 세우시고 \v 3 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너희에게 말한다. 너희가 돌이켜 어린아이들처럼 되지 않으면, 결코 천국에 들어가지 못할 것이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 어린아이 하나를 불러 그들 가운데 세우시고 \v 3 말씀하셨다. "진실로 너희에게 말한다. 너희가 돌이켜서 어린아이와 같이 되지 않으면, 절대로 천국에 들어가지 못한다.
ko.R: 예수께서 어린아이 하나를 가까이 부르셨다. 그리고 그 아이를 제자들 가운데 세우셨다. \v 3 그리고 말씀하셨다. "내가 분명히 말한다. 너희는 삶의 방향을 바꾸어 어린아이처럼 되어야 한다. 그렇지 않으면 결코 천국에 들어가지 못할 것이다.

decisions.choice: turn: change the direction of your life
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn. Here it means a change of heart and ways, away from the wish to be great.

decisions.choice: become like children: in their lowly place, not in their innocence
decisions.reason: Verse 4 explains the comparison: a child humbles himself. A child had no rank or power and depended on others. The point answers the disciples' question about rank.

decisions.choice: you will never enter: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together to make the denial as strong as possible. Those who seek rank are not merely low in the kingdom; they are outside it.

decisions.choice: the speech that begins here runs to 18:20
decisions.reason: Jesus's fourth long speech in Matthew begins here. After Peter's question in 18:21 it goes on to the end of the chapter.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 18:20
alternatives: closing and reopening the quotation at each sentence
decisions.reason: Verses 3-20 are one speech, so the quotation marks stay open to its end. Jesus speaks again from 18:22 to 18:35.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus at the start of the scene.

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of Jesus's single amen used through Matthew, recorded once in this passage. Jesus speaks to the disciples, so every plural "you" and its verb in the speech is the reader setting: ustedes forms (the default) or vosotros forms.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R), here and in 18:13, 18:18-19
decisions.reason: The forms settled for the New Testament and used in Mark and Luke.

decisions.choice: si vous ne changez pas (L); si vous ne changez pas de direction (B); vous devez changer (R)
alternatives: si vous ne vous convertissez pas
si vous ne vous retournez pas
decisions.reason: The verb means turning round, a change in the direction of one's life (m1). French "se retourner" would mean looking back, and "se convertir" now suggests changing religion; "changer" says it plainly, and Balanced keeps the picture of a road.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The rendering of Jesus's single amen used through Matthew, recorded once in this passage; John's double form is "Kweli kweli nawaambia".

decisions.choice: msipogeuka (unless you turn)
decisions.reason: The verb means to change the direction of one's life (meaning decision m1). "Kugeuka" keeps that picture in plain words; "kuongoka" is the church word for conversion and says more than the Greek does here.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với các con" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các con" (R), with "các con" for the disciples through 18:20
alternatives: "Quả thật, Ta nói với các con"
decisions.reason: The settled wording for Jesus's "amen" (Matthew 5:18, Mark 10:15); he speaks to his disciples as "các con" in the teaching that runs to 18:20.

decisions.choice: "quay lại" (L); "đổi hướng" (B); "thay đổi" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary one for turning around, not the word for repentance; each level keeps the picture of a change of direction in its own register.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 18:1-14; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, and Jesus speaks to the disciples in 해라체
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R), through chapter 18; "돌이키다" (L, B), "삶의 방향을 바꾸다" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled Korean form of "amen" for the Gospels. To turn is to change the direction of one's life (meaning decision); Readable says so in plain words.

decisions.choice: [가까이]
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is to call someone to oneself; Korean says that with "가까이 부르다", and Literal brackets the added word.

source.text: ὅστις οὖν ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὡς τὸ παιδίον τοῦτο, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ μείζων ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Whoever therefore will humble himself as the child this, he is the greater in the kingdom of the heavens;

en.L: Whoever therefore humbles {{gender:themselves|himself}} like this child, {{gender:that person|he}} is the greatest in the kingdom of the heavens;
en.B: So the greatest in the kingdom of heaven is anyone who takes a low place, as this child does.
en.R: The most important person in the kingdom of heaven is the one who stops trying to be important and becomes humble like this child.

es.L: Por tanto, quien se rebaje a sí mismo como este niño, {{gender:esa persona es la mayor|ese es el mayor}} en el reino de los cielos;
es.B: Así que el mayor en el reino de los cielos es quien ocupa un lugar humilde, como lo hace este niño.
es.R: La persona más importante en el reino de los cielos es la que deja de querer ser importante y se hace humilde como este niño.

fr.L: Quiconque donc s’abaissera comme cet enfant, c’est lui le plus grand dans le royaume des cieux ;
fr.B: Ainsi, le plus grand dans le royaume des cieux, c’est celui qui prend la dernière place, comme cet enfant.
fr.R: Le plus important dans le royaume des cieux, c’est celui qui ne cherche plus à être important et qui accepte d’être petit, comme cet enfant.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo mtu yeyote atakayejishusha kama mtoto huyu, yeye ni mkubwa zaidi katika ufalme wa mbinguni;
sw.B: Kwa hiyo aliye mkubwa zaidi katika ufalme wa mbinguni ni yeyote anayekubali nafasi ya chini, kama mtoto huyu anavyofanya.
sw.R: Mtu aliye muhimu kuliko wote katika ufalme wa mbinguni ni yule anayeacha kujifanya mtu muhimu, akawa mnyenyekevu kama mtoto huyu.

vi.L: Vậy ai hạ mình xuống như đứa trẻ này, người ấy là người lớn hơn cả trong vương quốc thiên đàng;
vi.B: Vậy ai tự hạ mình xuống như em nhỏ này, người ấy là người lớn nhất trong vương quốc thiên đàng.
vi.R: Ai thôi tìm cách làm người quan trọng và chịu khiêm nhường như em nhỏ này, thì người ấy là người quan trọng nhất trong vương quốc thiên đàng.

ko.L: 그러므로 누구든지 이 어린아이처럼 자기를 낮추는 사람, 그 사람이 천국에서 더 큰 사람이다.
ko.B: 그러니 이 어린아이처럼 스스로 낮은 자리에 서는 사람이 천국에서 가장 큰 사람이다.
ko.R: 이 어린아이처럼 높아지려고 애쓰지 않고 자기를 낮추는 사람이 천국에서 가장 높은 사람이다.

decisions.choice: humbles himself: takes a low place of his own will
decisions.reason: The verb means to make low. A child had no standing in the society of the time; the disciple chooses that low place instead of seeking rank (23:12).

decisions.choice: like this child: as low as this child, not as humble as this child feels
alternatives: with the humble attitude of a child
decisions.reason: A child does not humble himself by choice. The comparison is with the child's position: the disciple makes himself as lowly as a child already is.

decisions.choice: the greatest: true greatness turns the disciples' idea of rank upside down
alternatives: a fixed order of rank in heaven
decisions.reason: Jesus answers their question, but not as they expected. The same reversal comes in 20:26-27.

decisions.choice: {{gender:themselves|himself}}; {{gender:that person|he}}
decisions.reason: The saying is for anyone, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: takes a low place (B); stops trying to be important and becomes humble (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what humbling oneself means here, following the meaning decisions.

decisions.choice: se rebaje a sí mismo
decisions.reason: The Greek means to take a low place of one's own will (meaning decision m1). In everyday Spanish "humillarse" is often heard as being humiliated, so Literal says "rebajarse"; Balanced says "ocupa un lugar humilde", as the English says "takes a low place".

decisions.choice: "Quiconque … s’abaissera … c’est lui", with no gender setting; the same in 18:6 ("pour lui", "son cou")
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs {{gender:themselves|himself}} and {{gender:that person|he}}. French "quiconque" already means anyone, and the "se" and "lui" that refer back to it are ordinary generic French, so the style guide puts no span on them.

decisions.choice: atakayejishusha (whoever lowers himself)
decisions.reason: The Greek means to take a low place of one's own will (meaning decision m1). "Kujishusha" (to lower oneself) keeps that picture; Balanced says "anayekubali nafasi ya chini", as the English says "takes a low place".

decisions.choice: mtu yeyote ... yeye, with no gender setting
alternatives: gender spans as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "themselves" or "himself". Swahili "mtu" and "yeye" already mean any man or woman, so the setting has nothing to change, here or in verses 6-7.

decisions.choice: "hạ mình xuống" (L), "tự hạ mình xuống" (B); "người ấy" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "hạ mình" keeps the picture of taking a low place by one's own choice; Vietnamese "ai ... người ấy" is already inclusive, so the English gender span has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "누구든지", "그 사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" and "누구든지" already include men and women, so the English gender spans have nothing to change (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: "자기를 낮추다" (L, R); "스스로 낮은 자리에 서다" (B)
decisions.reason: To humble oneself is to take a low place of one's own will (meaning decision); Balanced says it with the picture of the lowly place, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται ἓν παιδίον τοιοῦτο ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐμὲ δέχεται.

records.literal_gloss: And whoever if receives one child such in the name of me, me receives.

en.L: And whoever receives one such child in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name receives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: And when someone welcomes a child like this for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sake, it is {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they welcome.
en.R: And when people welcome a child like this because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are welcoming {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Y quien acoja a uno de tales niños en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me acoge.
es.B: Y cuando alguien da la bienvenida a un niño como este por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, es a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} a quien recibe.
es.R: Y cuando las personas reciben bien a un niño como este por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} me están recibiendo.

fr.L: Et quiconque reçoit un seul enfant tel que celui-ci en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} reçoit.
fr.B: Et celui qui accueille un enfant comme celui-ci par amour pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’il accueille.
fr.R: Quand quelqu’un accueille un enfant comme celui-ci à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qu’il accueille.

sw.L: Na yeyote atakayemkaribisha mtoto mmoja wa namna hii kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, ananikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.B: Na mtu anapomkaribisha mtoto kama huyu kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} anayenikaribisha.
sw.R: Na watu wanapomkaribisha mtoto kama huyu kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, wananikaribisha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.

vi.L: Và ai nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tiếp nhận một đứa trẻ như thế này là tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Ai vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà tiếp đón một em nhỏ như em này là tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Khi ai vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà tiếp đón một em nhỏ như em này, người ấy đang tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그리고 누구든지 내 이름으로 이런 어린아이 하나를 영접하면, 나를 영접하는 것이다.
ko.B: 누구든지 내 이름으로 이런 어린아이 하나를 맞아들이면, 나를 맞아들이는 것이다.
ko.R: 누구든지 나를 위해서 이런 어린아이 하나를 반갑게 맞아 주면, 그것은 나를 맞아 주는 것이다.

decisions.choice: in my name: because of me, as one who belongs to me
decisions.reason: The phrase gives the reason for the welcome. The child is received for Jesus's sake (compare 10:40-42).

decisions.choice: one such child: a real child, and those who are lowly like one
decisions.reason: The child stands in front of them, but "such" points also to disciples who have made themselves low (18:4). Verse 6 moves on to "these little ones who believe in me".

decisions.choice: receive: welcome as a guest and care for
decisions.reason: The verb is used of welcoming people into one's home (10:14, 40). Caring for the lowly is caring for Jesus himself (25:40).

decisions.choice: for my sake (B); because of me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means, following the meaning decision. Literal keeps "in my name".

decisions.choice: kumkaribisha (to welcome)
decisions.reason: The verb means to welcome as a guest and care for (meaning decision m3). "Kukaribisha" is the word for welcoming a guest; "kupokea" can mean merely to receive a thing.

decisions.choice: "tiếp nhận" (L); "tiếp đón" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 9:37 and Matthew 10:14: receiving as a guest is "tiếp đón"; Literal keeps the more general word.

decisions.choice: "영접하다" (L); "맞아들이다" (B); "반갑게 맞아 주다" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the parallel Mark 9:37 in Korean: to receive is to welcome as a guest (meaning decision).

source.text: Ὃς δ’ ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ, συμφέρει αὐτῷ ἵνα κρεμασθῇ μύλος ὀνικὸς εἰς τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ καταποντισθῇ ἐν τῷ πελάγει τῆς θαλάσσης.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever but if causes to stumble one of the little ones these the believing in me, it is better for him that be hung a millstone of a donkey around the neck of him and he be drowned in the depth of the sea.

en.L: But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to stumble, it would be better for {{gender:them|him}} to have a donkey's millstone hung around {{gender:their|his}} neck and to be drowned in the depth of the sea.
en.B: But if anyone leads into sin one of these little ones who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that person would be better off sunk far out at sea with a great millstone fastened around their neck.
en.R: These little ones believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. If anyone makes one of them sin, it would be better for that person to be thrown into the deep sea with a huge stone tied around their neck.

es.L: Pero a quien haga tropezar a uno de estos pequeños que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, más le valdría que le colgaran al cuello una muela de molino de asno y que fuera ahogado en la profundidad del mar.
es.B: Pero si alguien hace caer en pecado a uno de estos pequeños que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, mejor le sería ser hundido en alta mar con una gran piedra de molino atada al cuello.
es.R: Estos pequeños creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Si alguien hace pecar a uno de ellos, sería mejor para esa persona que la tiraran al mar profundo con una piedra enorme atada al cuello.

fr.L: Mais quiconque fera trébucher un seul de ces petits qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, il vaut mieux pour lui qu’on lui suspende au cou une meule d’âne et qu’il soit englouti dans les profondeurs de la mer.
fr.B: Mais si quelqu’un entraîne dans le péché l’un de ces petits qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, mieux vaudrait pour lui être englouti en pleine mer avec une grosse meule attachée au cou.
fr.R: Ces petits croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Si quelqu’un pousse l’un d’eux à pécher, il vaudrait mieux pour lui qu’on le jette au fond de la mer avec une énorme pierre attachée autour du cou.

sw.L: Lakini mtu yeyote atakayemsababisha mmoja wa hawa wadogo wanaoniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ajikwae, ni afadhali kwake atundikwe shingoni jiwe la kusagia la punda, azamishwe katikati ya bahari yenye kina kirefu.
sw.B: Lakini mtu akimsababisha mmoja wa wadogo hawa wanaoniamini kuanguka dhambini, ingekuwa heri kwake kuzamishwa mbali baharini akiwa amefungwa jiwe kubwa la kusagia shingoni.
sw.R: Wadogo hawa wananiamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Mtu akimfanya mmoja wao atende dhambi, ingekuwa afadhali kwake atupwe katika bahari yenye kina kirefu akiwa amefungwa jiwe kubwa shingoni.

vi.L: Nhưng ai làm cho một trong những kẻ nhỏ này, là những người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vấp ngã, thì thà người ấy bị treo cối đá [do] lừa [kéo] vào cổ mình và bị nhận chìm dưới lòng biển sâu còn tốt hơn cho người ấy.
vi.B: Còn ai khiến một trong những người nhỏ bé này, là những người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, phải sa ngã, thì thà người ấy bị buộc một cối đá lớn vào cổ rồi bị nhận chìm giữa biển sâu còn hơn.
vi.R: Những người nhỏ bé này tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Nếu ai khiến một người trong họ phạm tội, thì thà người ấy bị buộc một tảng đá xay rất nặng vào cổ rồi bị ném xuống biển sâu còn tốt hơn.

ko.L: 그러나 누구든지 나를 믿는 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나를 걸려 넘어지게 하면, 연자 맷돌이 그의 목에 매달려 바다 깊은 곳에 가라앉는 것이 그에게 더 낫다.
ko.B: 그러나 나를 믿는 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나라도 죄짓게 하는 사람은, 차라리 큰 맷돌을 목에 매달고 깊은 바다에 빠지는 편이 더 낫다.
ko.R: 이 작은 사람들은 나를 믿는다. 누구든지 그들 가운데 하나라도 죄를 짓게 만들면, 그 사람은 아주 무거운 맷돌을 목에 매달고 깊은 바다에 던져지는 것이 더 낫다.

decisions.choice: causes to stumble: leads into sin, so as to fall away from faith
decisions.reason: As in 5:29, the verb pictures a trap or a stone that trips someone. Here it means leading a believer into sin or away from following Jesus.

decisions.choice: these little ones who believe in me: Jesus's disciples, lowly in the world's eyes
decisions.reason: "Who believe in me" shows that believers are meant, as in 10:42. The child of 18:2 stands for them.

decisions.choice: a donkey's millstone: the heavy upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey
decisions.reason: Most grinding was done with small stones turned by hand. This is the large stone of a mill worked by an animal, far too heavy to swim with.

decisions.choice: it would be better for him: what awaits him is worse than drowning
alternatives: a punishment the church should carry out
decisions.reason: Jesus does not command anyone to be drowned. He says that a terrible death would be better than the judgment that faces one who ruins a believer.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}; {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The warning is for anyone, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: leads into sin (B); makes one of them sin (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:29, Balanced and Readable say what the picture means.

decisions.choice: These little ones believe in me. (first)
alternatives: one of these little ones who believe in me
decisions.reason: Readable says first who the little ones are, then gives the warning.

decisions.choice: le ... su cuello, with no gender setting
alternatives: gender spans as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "them" or "him". Spanish "quien" and "le" already speak of any man or woman, so the setting has nothing to change here or in verse 7, where only "la persona" and "el hombre" differ.

decisions.choice: faire trébucher (L), here and in 18:8-9
decisions.reason: As Mark 9:42: French "scandaliser" now means to shock or offend, which is not the sense here (m1). "Faire trébucher" keeps the picture of the Greek; Balanced and Readable say what the stumbling is, as the English does.

decisions.choice: jiwe la kusagia la punda
decisions.reason: The Greek names the heavy upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "la punda"; Balanced and Readable say how big it is, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "làm cho ... vấp ngã" (L); "khiến ... sa ngã" (B); "khiến ... phạm tội" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of Mark 9:42 and Matthew 5:29 at each level, kept through 18:6-9.

decisions.choice: "cối đá [do] lừa [kéo]" (L); "cối đá lớn" (B); "tảng đá xay rất nặng" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 9:42: Literal shows the donkey-driven millstone with supplied words; Balanced and Readable give its size and weight.

decisions.choice: "걸려 넘어지게 하다" (L), "죄짓게 하다" (B, R), through 18:9; "연자 맷돌" (L), "큰 맷돌" (B), "아주 무거운 맷돌" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the parallel Mark 9:42 and of the Korean Matthew 5:29-30. A "연자 맷돌" is the Korean name for a large millstone turned by an animal, which is what the donkey's millstone was (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "그", "그 사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean refers to the person without a gendered pronoun (style guide, section 7).

source.text: οὐαὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ἀπὸ τῶν σκανδάλων· ἀνάγκη γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τὰ σκάνδαλα, πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ δι’ οὗ τὸ σκάνδαλον ἔρχεται.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to the world because of the stumbling blocks; necessary for to come the stumbling blocks, but woe to the man through whom the stumbling block comes.

en.L: Woe to the world because of the causes of stumbling! For it is necessary that causes of stumbling come, but woe to the {{gender:person|man}} through whom the cause of stumbling comes!
en.B: Woe to the world for the snares that trip people into sin! Such snares are sure to come, but woe to anyone who brings one about!
en.R: How terrible it will be for the people of the world because of the things that make people sin! These things will surely happen. But how terrible it will be for anyone who causes them!

es.L: ¡Ay del mundo por las ocasiones de caída! Porque es necesario que vengan las ocasiones de caída, pero ¡ay {{gender:de la persona|del hombre}} por quien viene la ocasión de caída!
es.B: ¡Ay del mundo por las trampas que hacen caer a la gente en el pecado! Tales trampas vendrán sin falta, pero ¡ay de quien las provoque!
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para la gente del mundo por las cosas que hacen pecar a las personas! Esas cosas sin duda sucederán. ¡Pero qué terrible será para quien las cause!

fr.L: Malheur au monde à cause des pierres d’achoppement ! Car il est nécessaire que viennent les pierres d’achoppement, mais malheur à {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} par qui la pierre d’achoppement vient !
fr.B: Malheur au monde à cause des pièges qui font tomber les gens dans le péché ! Ces pièges viendront forcément, mais malheur à celui qui en est la cause !
fr.R: Ce sera terrible pour les gens du monde, à cause de tout ce qui fait tomber dans le péché ! Ces choses arriveront, c’est sûr. Mais ce sera terrible pour celui qui en est la cause !

sw.L: Ole wa ulimwengu kwa sababu ya vikwazo! Kwa maana ni lazima vikwazo vije, lakini ole wake mtu ambaye kikwazo huja kupitia kwake!
sw.B: Ole wa ulimwengu kwa sababu ya mitego inayowanasa watu katika dhambi! Mitego hiyo haina budi kuja, lakini ole wake yeyote anayeileta!
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya sana kwa watu wa ulimwengu kwa sababu ya mambo yanayowafanya watu watende dhambi! Mambo hayo yatatokea tu. Lakini itakuwa vibaya sana kwa mtu yeyote anayeyasababisha!

vi.L: Khốn cho thế gian vì những cớ vấp ngã! Vì những cớ vấp ngã tất phải đến, nhưng khốn cho người mà cớ vấp ngã đến bởi người ấy!
vi.B: Khốn cho thế gian vì những cạm bẫy làm người ta sa vào tội lỗi! Những cạm bẫy ấy tất phải đến, nhưng khốn cho kẻ gây ra cạm bẫy!
vi.R: Thật khốn khổ cho người đời vì những điều khiến người ta phạm tội! Những điều ấy chắc chắn sẽ xảy ra. Nhưng thật khốn khổ cho người nào gây ra những điều ấy!

ko.L: 걸림돌들 때문에 세상에 화가 있다! 걸림돌들이 오는 것은 반드시 있어야 하는 일이지만, 걸림돌을 오게 하는 그 사람에게는 화가 있다!
ko.B: 사람을 죄에 빠뜨리는 올무들 때문에 세상은 얼마나 불행하냐! 그런 올무는 반드시 생기겠지만, 그것을 놓는 사람은 얼마나 불행하냐!
ko.R: 사람들을 죄짓게 하는 일들 때문에 세상 사람들에게 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다! 그런 일들은 반드시 생긴다. 그러나 그런 일을 일으키는 사람에게는 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다!

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning over coming judgment
decisions.reason: As in 11:21, the word both mourns and warns. Jesus speaks of the judgment that will fall.

decisions.choice: the world: humankind, which suffers from the things that lead to sin
decisions.reason: Here the world is the human race. The first woe pities it; the second falls on the one through whom the harm comes.

decisions.choice: necessary: such things are bound to happen in a fallen world
decisions.reason: That snares will come does not excuse the one who sets them. Matthew holds both sides together, as with Judas (26:24).

decisions.choice: stumbling blocks: whatever trips a person into sin
decisions.reason: The noun is related to the verb of 18:6. It first meant the trigger of a trap.

decisions.choice: Woe
decisions.reason: As in 11:21, Literal and Balanced keep the old word for a cry of judgment. Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}}
decisions.reason: The warning is for anyone, so the inclusive form is the default. Balanced and Readable say "anyone".

decisions.choice: the people of the world
decisions.reason: Readable says that the world here means people.

decisions.choice: ¡Ay ...! (L, B); ¡Qué terrible será ...! (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish: "¡ay!" is the cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m1). Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Malheur (L, B), ce sera terrible (R); pierres d’achoppement (L), pièges (B)
decisions.reason: "Malheur" is the style guide's word for the cry of judgment at Literal and Balanced; Readable follows the English "how terrible". "Pierres d’achoppement" is the word Luke 17:1 uses at Literal for the same Greek; "scandales" would now mean public outrages.

decisions.choice: ole (L, B); itakuwa vibaya sana (R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili: "ole" is the cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m1). Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Khốn cho" (L, B); "Thật khốn khổ cho" (R)
decisions.reason: "Khốn cho" is the familiar Vietnamese cry of woe and warning; Readable spells out the misery that is coming.

decisions.choice: "cớ vấp ngã" (L); "cạm bẫy" (B); "những điều khiến người ta phạm tội" (R); "người", "kẻ" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The noun matches the verb of 18:6 at Literal; Balanced uses the picture of a snare; Readable says what it does.

decisions.choice: "화가 있다" (L); "얼마나 불행하냐" (B); "끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다" (R) for ouai
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Matthew 11:21: Literal keeps the traditional words in a modern ending; Balanced and Readable say the grief and the warning (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "걸림돌" (L); "올무" (B); "죄짓게 하는 일" (R) for skandalon
decisions.reason: A stumbling block is whatever trips a person into sin (meaning decision); Literal keeps the picture of the stone, Balanced the picture of a snare, as the English does, and Readable says what it is. No gender span for "사람".

source.text: Εἰ δὲ ἡ χείρ σου ἢ ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ· καλόν σοί ἐστιν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν κυλλὸν ἢ χωλόν, ἢ δύο χεῖρας ἢ δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: If but the hand of you or the foot of you causes to stumble you, cut off it and throw from you; good for you it is to enter into the life crippled or lame, than two hands or two feet having to be thrown into the fire the eternal.

en.L: And if your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw [it] away from you; it is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
en.B: If your hand or your foot leads you into sin, cut it off and get rid of it. You are better off entering life maimed or lame than keeping both hands or both feet and being thrown into the eternal fire.
en.R: If your hand or your foot makes you sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better to have life with God with only one hand or one foot than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.

es.L: Y si tu mano o tu pie te hace tropezar, córtalo y tíralo lejos de ti; es bueno para ti entrar en la vida lisiado o cojo, antes que, con dos manos o dos pies, ser echado al fuego eterno.
es.B: Si tu mano o tu pie te lleva a pecar, córtalo y deshazte de él. Más te vale entrar en la vida mutilado o cojo que conservar las dos manos o los dos pies y ser arrojado al fuego eterno.
es.R: Si tu mano o tu pie te hace pecar, córtalo y tíralo. Es mejor tener vida con Dios con una sola mano o un solo pie que tener dos manos y dos pies y ser echado al fuego eterno.

fr.L: Et si ta main ou ton pied te fait trébucher, coupe-le et jette-le loin de toi ; il est bon pour toi d’entrer dans la vie estropié ou boiteux, plutôt que d’avoir deux mains ou deux pieds et d’être jeté dans le feu éternel.
fr.B: Si ta main ou ton pied t’entraîne dans le péché, coupe-le et débarrasse-t’en. Mieux vaut pour toi entrer dans la vie mutilé ou boiteux que de garder tes deux mains ou tes deux pieds et d’être jeté dans le feu éternel.
fr.R: Si ta main ou ton pied te fait pécher, coupe-le et jette-le. Il vaut mieux n’avoir qu’une main ou qu’un pied et vivre avec Dieu que d’avoir deux mains et deux pieds et d’être jeté dans le feu éternel.

sw.L: Na ikiwa mkono wako au mguu wako unakuangusha, uukate na kuutupilia mbali; ni vyema kwako kuingia uzimani ukiwa umelemaa au unachechemea, kuliko kutupwa katika moto wa milele ukiwa na mikono yote miwili au miguu yote miwili.
sw.B: Mkono wako au mguu wako ukikuongoza kutenda dhambi, ukate na kuutupa mbali. Ni bora kwako kuingia uzimani ukiwa umekatwa kiungo au ukichechemea, kuliko kubaki na mikono yote miwili au miguu yote miwili na kutupwa katika moto wa milele.
sw.R: Mkono wako au mguu wako ukikufanya utende dhambi, ukate na kuutupa. Ni afadhali kuwa na uzima pamoja na Mungu ukiwa na mkono mmoja au mguu mmoja, kuliko kuwa na mikono miwili na miguu miwili na kutupwa katika moto wa milele.

vi.L: Và nếu tay con hoặc chân con làm cho con vấp ngã, hãy chặt nó đi và ném xa khỏi con; con vào sự sống mà tàn tật hoặc què quặt thì tốt cho con hơn là có hai tay hoặc hai chân mà bị ném vào lửa đời đời.
vi.B: Nếu tay hay chân con khiến con sa ngã, hãy chặt nó đi và vứt xa khỏi con. Thà con bị cụt tay hay què chân mà vào sự sống, còn hơn là có đủ hai tay hai chân mà bị ném vào lửa đời đời.
vi.R: Nếu tay hay chân con khiến con phạm tội, hãy chặt nó đi và ném xa khỏi con. Thà con chỉ còn một tay hay một chân mà được sống với Đức Chúa Trời, còn hơn là có đủ hai tay hai chân mà bị ném vào lửa cháy đời đời.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 네 손이나 네 발이 너를 걸려 넘어지게 하면, 그것을 잘라 네게서 내던져라. 두 손이나 두 발을 가지고 영원한 불에 던져지는 것보다, 불구가 되거나 다리를 저는 채로 생명에 들어가는 것이 네게 더 낫다.
ko.B: 네 손이나 발이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그것을 잘라 내버려라. 두 손이나 두 발을 다 가지고 영원한 불에 던져지는 것보다, 장애를 입은 몸이나 다리를 저는 몸으로 생명에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다.
ko.R: 네 손이나 발이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그것을 잘라 던져 버려라. 두 손과 두 발을 다 가지고 영원한 불에 던져지는 것보다, 손 하나나 발 하나만 가지고 하나님과 함께하는 생명에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다.

decisions.choice: cut off: overstatement that demands drastic action against sin
alternatives: a command to harm the body
decisions.reason: As in 5:29-30, Jesus uses deliberate overstatement. The point is to deal ruthlessly with whatever leads to sin, because the stakes are eternal.

decisions.choice: enter life: enter eternal life in the kingdom
alternatives: go on living in this world
decisions.reason: Life is set against the eternal fire. Matthew uses "enter life" and "enter the kingdom" for the same thing (19:17, 23).

decisions.choice: the eternal fire: the fire of final judgment, which does not end
alternatives: a fire that lasts a long time
decisions.reason: The word means belonging to the age to come and so without end. Matthew uses the same phrase in 25:41 and sets eternal punishment against eternal life in 25:46.

decisions.choice: causes you to stumble: leads you into sin
decisions.reason: As in 5:29. In 18:6-7 others cause the stumbling; here a person's own hand or foot does.

decisions.choice: leads you into sin (B); makes you sin (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:29-30, Balanced and Readable say what the picture means.

decisions.choice: have life with God
decisions.reason: Readable says what life is meant, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: tú forms, with no plural_you setting (verses 8-9)
decisions.reason: Here Jesus speaks to each hearer in the singular, so Spanish uses "tú" ("tu mano", "córtalo"), which is the same in Latin America and Spain and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: uzima (life)
decisions.reason: Life here is eternal life in the kingdom (meaning decision m2). "Uzima" is life itself, the word of "uzima wa milele"; "maisha" is a lifetime or daily living. The same in verse 9.

decisions.choice: kuliko kutupwa ... ukiwa na mikono yote miwili
alternatives: kuliko kuwa na mikono miwili ... na kutupwa
decisions.reason: Swahili reads more clearly with the main verb first, so Literal puts "being thrown" before "having two hands"; the Greek has the participle first. The same in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "con" for the singular "you" in 18:8-9
decisions.reason: The Greek turns to a singular "you"; as in Matthew 5:29-30, Jesus speaks to each hearer as "con".

decisions.choice: "được sống với Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 9:43 and the English Readable: the life meant is eternal life with God.

decisions.choice: "생명에 들어가다" (L, B); "하나님과 함께하는 생명에 들어가다" (R); "불구" (L), "장애를 입은 몸" (B)
decisions.reason: The wording of the Korean Mark 9:43-45: to enter life is to enter eternal life in the kingdom (meaning decision), which Readable makes plain. Balanced uses the respectful modern phrase for disability.

source.text: καὶ εἰ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ· καλόν σοί ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν, ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.

records.literal_gloss: And if the eye of you causes to stumble you, tear out it and throw from you; good for you it is one-eyed into the life to enter, than two eyes having to be thrown into the Gehenna of the fire.

en.L: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw [it] away from you; it is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the Gehenna of fire.
en.B: And if your eye leads you into sin, pull it out and get rid of it. You are better off entering life with one eye than keeping both eyes and being thrown into the fire of hell.
en.R: If your eye makes you sin, pull it out and throw it away. It is better to have life with God with only one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.

es.L: Y si tu ojo te hace tropezar, sácalo y tíralo lejos de ti; es bueno para ti entrar tuerto en la vida, antes que, con dos ojos, ser echado a la Gehena del fuego.
es.B: Y si tu ojo te lleva a pecar, arráncalo y deshazte de él. Más te vale entrar en la vida con un solo ojo que conservar los dos ojos y ser arrojado al fuego del infierno.
es.R: Si tu ojo te hace pecar, sácalo y tíralo. Es mejor tener vida con Dios con un solo ojo que tener dos ojos y ser echado al fuego del infierno.

fr.L: Et si ton œil te fait trébucher, arrache-le et jette-le loin de toi ; il est bon pour toi d’entrer dans la vie borgne, plutôt que d’avoir deux yeux et d’être jeté dans la géhenne du feu.
fr.B: Et si ton œil t’entraîne dans le péché, arrache-le et débarrasse-t’en. Mieux vaut pour toi entrer dans la vie avec un seul œil que de garder tes deux yeux et d’être jeté dans le feu de l’enfer.
fr.R: Si ton œil te fait pécher, arrache-le et jette-le. Il vaut mieux n’avoir qu’un œil et vivre avec Dieu que d’avoir deux yeux et d’être jeté dans le feu de l’enfer.

sw.L: Na jicho lako likikuangusha, ling'oe na kulitupilia mbali; ni vyema kwako kuingia uzimani ukiwa na jicho moja, kuliko kutupwa katika Gehena ya moto ukiwa na macho yote mawili.
sw.B: Na jicho lako likikuongoza kutenda dhambi, ling'oe na kulitupa mbali. Ni bora kwako kuingia uzimani ukiwa na jicho moja, kuliko kubaki na macho yote mawili na kutupwa katika moto wa jehanamu.
sw.R: Jicho lako likikufanya utende dhambi, ling'oe na kulitupa. Ni afadhali kuwa na uzima pamoja na Mungu ukiwa na jicho moja, kuliko kuwa na macho mawili na kutupwa katika moto wa jehanamu.

vi.L: Và nếu mắt con làm cho con vấp ngã, hãy móc nó ra và ném xa khỏi con; con vào sự sống mà chỉ có một mắt thì tốt cho con hơn là có hai mắt mà bị ném vào Ghê-hen-na lửa.
vi.B: Nếu mắt con khiến con sa ngã, hãy móc nó ra và vứt xa khỏi con. Thà con chỉ còn một mắt mà vào sự sống, còn hơn là có đủ hai mắt mà bị ném vào lửa địa ngục.
vi.R: Nếu mắt con khiến con phạm tội, hãy móc nó ra và ném đi. Thà con chỉ còn một mắt mà được sống với Đức Chúa Trời, còn hơn là có đủ hai mắt mà bị ném vào lửa địa ngục.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 네 눈이 너를 걸려 넘어지게 하면, 그것을 빼어 네게서 내던져라. 두 눈을 가지고 불의 게헨나에 던져지는 것보다, 한 눈으로 생명에 들어가는 것이 네게 더 낫다.
ko.B: 네 눈이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그 눈을 빼어 내버려라. 두 눈을 다 가지고 지옥 불에 던져지는 것보다, 한 눈만 가지고 생명에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다.
ko.R: 네 눈이 너를 죄짓게 하면, 그 눈을 빼서 던져 버려라. 두 눈을 다 가지고 지옥 불에 던져지는 것보다, 한 눈만 가지고 하나님과 함께하는 생명에 들어가는 것이 더 낫다.

decisions.choice: tear out: overstatement that demands drastic action against sin
alternatives: a command to harm the body
decisions.reason: As in 5:29 and 18:8.

decisions.choice: the Gehenna of fire: the place of final judgment
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, Gehenna was the valley of Hinnom by Jerusalem, whose name became a name for the fire of God's judgment. Here it stands in place of "the eternal fire" of 18:8.

decisions.choice: Gehenna (L); hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:22 and 5:29, Literal keeps the place name and Balanced and Readable use the word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: leads you into sin (B); makes you sin (R)
decisions.reason: As in 18:8.

decisions.choice: Gehena (L); el infierno (B, R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Spanish, as the English: Literal keeps the name of the place of final judgment (meaning decision m2), and Balanced and Readable say "infierno".

decisions.choice: la géhenne (L); l’enfer (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide and Mark 9:43: Literal keeps the place name, lowercase as the common French spelling; Balanced and Readable use the French word for the place of final judgment, as the English says "hell".

decisions.choice: Gehena (L); jehanamu (B, R)
decisions.reason: The New Testament choice for Swahili, as the English: Literal keeps the name of the place of final judgment (meaning decision m2), and Balanced and Readable say "jehanamu".

decisions.choice: "Ghê-hen-na" (L); "địa ngục" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 5:29 and 10:28 and Mark 9:43-47.

decisions.choice: "불의 게헨나" (L); "지옥 불" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As settled for the Korean Matthew (5:22, 5:29): Literal keeps the name Gehenna, Balanced and Readable use "지옥".

source.text: Ὁρᾶτε μὴ καταφρονήσητε ἑνὸς τῶν μικρῶν τούτων, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτῶν ἐν οὐρανοῖς διὰ παντὸς βλέπουσι τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: See not you despise one of the little ones these, I say for to you that the angels of them in heavens continually see the face of the Father of me the in heavens.

en.L: See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that their angels in [the] heavens always see the face of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who [is] in [the] heavens.
en.B: Take care never to look down on a single one of these little ones. I tell you, their angels in heaven stand always in the presence of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven.
en.R: Be careful that you do not think any of these little ones are unimportant. I tell you, they have angels in heaven who are always with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado de no despreciar a uno solo de estos pequeños; porque {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que en [los] cielos los ángeles de ellos contemplan continuamente el rostro de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre, el que [está] en [los] cielos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Cuídense|Cuidaos}} de no mirar nunca con desprecio a ninguno de estos pequeños. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que sus ángeles en el cielo están siempre en la presencia de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre que está en el cielo.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado de no pensar que alguno de estos pequeños no es importante. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que ellos tienen ángeles en el cielo que están siempre con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre que está en el cielo.

fr.L: Gardez-vous de mépriser un seul de ces petits, car je vous dis que leurs anges dans les cieux voient continuellement la face de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui [est] dans les cieux.
fr.B: Prenez garde de ne jamais mépriser un seul de ces petits. Je vous le dis, leurs anges dans le ciel se tiennent sans cesse en présence de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est dans le ciel.
fr.R: Faites attention : ne pensez jamais qu’un seul de ces petits n’a pas d’importance. Je vous le dis, ils ont des anges dans le ciel qui sont toujours auprès de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père qui est au ciel.

sw.L: Jihadharini msije mkamdharau hata mmoja wa wadogo hawa; kwa maana nawaambia, malaika wao mbinguni wanauona uso wa Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni wakati wote.
sw.B: Jihadharini msimdharau kamwe hata mmoja wa wadogo hawa. Nawaambia, malaika wao mbinguni husimama daima mbele za Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni.
sw.R: Kuweni waangalifu msidhani kwamba yeyote kati ya wadogo hawa si muhimu. Nawaambia, wao wana malaika mbinguni ambao wako daima pamoja na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} aliye mbinguni.

vi.L: Hãy coi chừng, đừng khinh dể một ai trong những kẻ nhỏ này, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con rằng các thiên sứ của họ ở trên các tầng trời luôn luôn nhìn thấy mặt Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, Đấng ở trên các tầng trời.
vi.B: Hãy cẩn thận, đừng bao giờ coi thường một người nào trong những người nhỏ bé này. Ta nói với các con, các thiên sứ của họ ở trên trời luôn luôn được đứng trước mặt Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở trên trời.
vi.R: Hãy cẩn thận, đừng bao giờ nghĩ rằng một người nào trong những người nhỏ bé này là không quan trọng. Ta nói với các con, họ có các thiên sứ ở trên trời, là những thiên sứ luôn luôn ở với Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trên trời.

ko.L: 너희는 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나라도 업신여기지 않도록 조심하여라. 내가 너희에게 말한다. 하늘들에 있는 그들의 천사들이 하늘들에 계신 내 아버지의 얼굴을 항상 뵙고 있다.
ko.B: 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나라도 업신여기지 않도록 조심하여라. 내가 너희에게 말한다. 하늘에 있는 그들의 천사들은 하늘에 계신 내 아버지 앞에 늘 서 있다.
ko.R: 이 작은 사람들 가운데 누구라도 하찮게 여기지 않도록 조심하여라. 내가 너희에게 말한다. 그들에게는 하늘에 천사들이 있다. 그 천사들은 하늘에 계신 내 아버지와 늘 함께 있다.

decisions.choice: their angels: angels who care for the little ones
decisions.reason: Scripture speaks of angels sent to guard God's people (Psalm 91:11; Hebrews 1:14), and Acts 12:15 shows the belief that a person had an angel. The verse does not say more about how this is arranged.

decisions.choice: see the face: stand in the presence, with access to the king
decisions.reason: Those who saw the king's face were his closest servants, who could come before him at any time (2 Samuel 14:24; Esther 1:14). The little ones may seem of no account, but their angels have the Father's ear.

decisions.choice: no verse 11, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "For the Son of Man came to save the lost," added as verse 11 in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts go straight from verse 10 to verse 12. Many later ones add a verse very like Luke 19:10, probably taken from there to lead into the parable of the lost sheep. Older translations print it as verse 11. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: despise: treat as worthless, look down on
decisions.reason: The verb means to think little of someone. The little ones are easy to overlook because they have no rank.

decisions.choice: stand always in the presence of (B); are always with (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means, following the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}}; {{plural_you:les|os}}
decisions.reason: After the singular of verses 8-9, Jesus speaks to the disciples again in the plural, so the ustedes / vosotros setting returns and holds through verse 14.

decisions.choice: "Cha Ta, Đấng ở trên các tầng trời" (L); "Cha Ta ở trên trời" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As settled for Matthew (5:16, 10:32, 12:50).

decisions.choice: "được đứng trước mặt" (B)
decisions.reason: To see a king's face is to have access to him; Balanced says so, Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: "하늘들에" (L); "하늘에" (B, R) for "in the heavens"; "하늘에 계신 내 아버지"
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Matthew 5:16 and 12:50: Literal keeps the Greek plural, Balanced and Readable say "in heaven".

decisions.choice: "얼굴을 뵙다" (L); "앞에 서 있다" (B); "함께 있다" (R)
decisions.reason: To see the face is to stand in the presence of the king (meaning decision); Literal keeps the picture with the humble verb "뵙다" used of seeing a superior, and Balanced says what it means.

fr.B: Dites-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ce que vous en pensez.

vi.R: Các con hãy suy nghĩ điều này.

decisions.choice: what do you think: an invitation to judge the case that follows
alternatives: a request for opinions in general
decisions.reason: Jesus asks his hearers to judge from what they know, as in 17:25 and 21:28.

decisions.choice: Tell me what you think (B); Think about this (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the question into an invitation, which is how it works.

decisions.choice: Dites-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies "tell me"; the pronoun is Jesus speaking of himself, so French gives it the deity_pronoun span, as the style guide asks wherever a pronoun stands for Christ, though the English "me" here has none.

source.text: ἐὰν γένηταί τινι ἀνθρώπῳ ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ πλανηθῇ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν, οὐχὶ ἀφήσει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη καὶ πορευθεὶς ζητεῖ τὸ πλανώμενον;

records.literal_gloss: If there be to any man a hundred sheep and goes astray one of them, not will he leave the ninety nine on the mountains and having gone seek the straying?

en.L: If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go and look for the one that is straying?
en.B: Suppose someone owns a hundred sheep, and one of them wanders off. Will the owner not leave the ninety-nine on the hillsides and set out to search for the one that strayed?
en.R: Suppose someone has a hundred sheep and one of them wanders away. The owner will leave the other ninety-nine sheep on the hills and go to look for the lost one.

es.L: Si un hombre tiene cien ovejas y una de ellas se extravía, ¿no dejará las noventa y nueve en los montes e irá a buscar la que anda extraviada?
es.B: Supongamos que alguien tiene cien ovejas y una de ellas se pierde. ¿No dejará el dueño las noventa y nueve en las laderas y saldrá a buscar la que se extravió?
es.R: Supongamos que alguien tiene cien ovejas y una de ellas se pierde. El dueño dejará las otras noventa y nueve ovejas en los cerros e irá a buscar la oveja perdida.

fr.L: Si un homme a cent brebis et que l’une d’elles s’égare, ne laissera-t-il pas les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf sur les montagnes pour aller chercher celle qui s’égare ?
fr.B: Supposons que quelqu’un possède cent brebis et que l’une d’elles s’éloigne. Ne laissera-t-il pas les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf sur les collines pour partir à la recherche de celle qui s’est égarée ?
fr.R: Imaginez que quelqu’un ait cent moutons et que l’un d’eux se perde. Il va laisser les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf autres moutons sur les collines et partir chercher celui qui est perdu.

sw.L: Ikiwa mtu ana kondoo mia moja, na mmoja wao akapotea, je, hatawaacha wale tisini na tisa milimani, akaenda kumtafuta yule anayetangatanga?
sw.B: Tuseme mtu ana kondoo mia moja, na mmoja wao akapotea. Je, mwenye kondoo hatawaacha wale tisini na tisa kwenye vilima, aende kumtafuta yule aliyepotea?
sw.R: Tuseme mtu ana kondoo mia moja na mmoja wao anapotea. Mwenye kondoo atawaacha wale kondoo wengine tisini na tisa vilimani, aende kumtafuta yule aliyepotea.

vi.L: Nếu một người nào có một trăm con chiên và một con trong số đó đi lạc, chẳng lẽ người ấy không để chín mươi chín con lại trên núi mà đi tìm con chiên đi lạc sao?
vi.B: Giả sử có người có một trăm con chiên, và một con đi lạc mất. Chẳng lẽ người chủ lại không để chín mươi chín con kia trên sườn đồi mà lên đường đi tìm con chiên đi lạc sao?
vi.R: Giả sử có người có một trăm con chiên, và một con đi lạc. Người chủ sẽ để chín mươi chín con kia lại trên đồi và đi tìm con chiên bị lạc.

ko.L: 만일 어떤 사람에게 양 백 마리가 있는데 그 가운데 하나가 길을 잃으면, 그가 아흔아홉 마리를 산에 남겨 두고 가서 길을 잃은 것을 찾지 않겠느냐?
ko.B: 어떤 사람에게 양 백 마리가 있는데 그 가운데 한 마리가 길을 잃었다고 하자. 그러면 그 사람은 아흔아홉 마리를 산에 남겨 두고 길 잃은 양을 찾아 나서지 않겠느냐?
ko.R: 어떤 사람에게 양 백 마리가 있었는데, 그 가운데 한 마리가 길을 잃었다고 하자. 양 주인은 아흔아홉 마리를 언덕에 남겨 두고, 길 잃은 양을 찾으러 갈 것이다.

decisions.choice: will he not leave: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The Greek form shows that any owner would go looking. Leaving the flock on the open hills was a risk worth taking for the one lost sheep.

decisions.choice: the straying sheep: Ezekiel 34:11-16
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel God promises to seek out his scattered sheep himself and bring back the strays. Luke 15:3-7 tells the same parable about sinners who repent; here it is about a believer who wanders.

decisions.choice: go astray: wander away and be lost
decisions.reason: The verb means to wander off the right way, and is used of being led into error (24:4-5, 11). The sheep is the little one who has been led to stumble (18:6).

decisions.choice: a man (L); someone, the owner (B, R), with no gender or deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The owner is a figure in a picture, so the pronouns take no span. Balanced and Readable avoid naming a man, since the point is what any owner would do.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Will he not leave the ninety-nine?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes"; Readable gives the answer.

decisions.choice: hillsides (B); hills (R)
decisions.reason: The word covers hill country as well as mountains, where sheep were grazed.

decisions.choice: brebis (L, B); moutons (R)
decisions.reason: As Luke 15:4: "brebis" is the word French has long used for the sheep of a flock and keeps the link with the shepherd imagery of Scripture (m2); Readable says "moutons", the everyday word.

decisions.choice: "một người nào" (L); "có người", "người chủ" (B, R), with no gender or deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" is already inclusive; the owner is a figure in a picture, not a pronoun for God.

decisions.choice: "chẳng lẽ ... không ... sao?" for the question that expects "yes" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The modern Vietnamese form of a question expecting agreement; "há" is archaic.

decisions.choice: "어떤 사람", "양 주인" (R) with no gender span; "산" (L, B), "언덕" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" names no gender; the mountains are the hill country where sheep grazed, and Readable says "hills" as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν γένηται εὑρεῖν αὐτό, ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι χαίρει ἐπ’ αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα τοῖς μὴ πεπλανημένοις.

records.literal_gloss: And if it happens to find it, truly I say to you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety nine the not having gone astray.

en.L: And if he happens to find it, truly I tell you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
en.B: And if the owner does find it, truly I tell you, that one sheep brings more delight than the ninety-nine that never wandered off.
en.R: And if the owner finds it, I tell you the truth, the owner is happier about that one sheep than about the ninety-nine that did not wander away.

es.L: Y si llega a encontrarla, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que se alegra por ella más que por las noventa y nueve que no se extraviaron.
es.B: Y si el dueño logra encontrarla, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que esa oveja le da más alegría que las noventa y nueve que nunca se perdieron.
es.R: Y si el dueño la encuentra, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo la verdad: se pone más contento por esa oveja que por las noventa y nueve que no se perdieron.

fr.L: Et s’il arrive qu’il la trouve, en vérité, je vous le dis, il se réjouit à son sujet plus que pour les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf qui ne se sont pas égarées.
fr.B: Et s’il finit par la retrouver, en vérité, je vous le dis, cette seule brebis lui donne plus de joie que les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf qui ne se sont jamais égarées.
fr.R: Et s’il le retrouve, je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : il est plus heureux pour ce seul mouton que pour les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf qui ne s’étaient pas perdus.

sw.L: Na ikitokea kwamba amempata, kweli nawaambia, anamfurahia huyo kuliko wale tisini na tisa ambao hawakupotea.
sw.B: Na mwenye kondoo akimpata, kweli nawaambia, kondoo huyo mmoja humletea furaha kubwa kuliko wale tisini na tisa ambao hawakupotea kamwe.
sw.R: Na mwenye kondoo akimpata, nawaambia ukweli, atafurahi zaidi kwa sababu ya kondoo huyo mmoja kuliko kwa wale tisini na tisa ambao hawakupotea.

vi.L: Và nếu người ấy tìm được nó, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con rằng người ấy vui mừng vì nó hơn là vì chín mươi chín con không đi lạc.
vi.B: Và nếu người chủ tìm được nó, thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, người ấy vui mừng vì một con chiên ấy hơn là vì chín mươi chín con không hề đi lạc.
vi.R: Nếu người chủ tìm được con chiên ấy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói thật với các con, người ấy sẽ vui mừng vì một con chiên ấy hơn là vì chín mươi chín con không đi lạc.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 그가 그것을 찾게 되면, 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 그는 길을 잃지 않은 아흔아홉 마리보다 그 한 마리 때문에 더 기뻐한다.
ko.B: 그리고 그 양을 찾게 되면, 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 그는 길을 잃지 않은 아흔아홉 마리보다 그 한 마리 때문에 더 기뻐할 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 주인이 그 양을 찾으면, 길을 잃지 않은 아흔아홉 마리보다 찾은 한 마리 때문에 더 기뻐할 것이다.

decisions.choice: if he happens to find it: finding is not certain
decisions.reason: The words leave room for the search to fail. That makes the joy of finding greater, and it fits the warning of 18:14 that a little one could perish.

decisions.choice: rejoices more: the joy of finding what was lost
decisions.reason: The others are not loved less. The joy over the one that is found back is the stronger feeling of the moment.

decisions.choice: truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 18:3.

decisions.choice: that one sheep brings more delight
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the sheep the subject to keep the sentence short.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói thật với các con" (R) in mid-sentence
alternatives: "Ta nói thật với các con" at the start
decisions.reason: The Readable form of Jesus's "amen", kept where the Greek puts it, with the setting span because it stands inside the sentence (as Matthew 10:42).

decisions.choice: "내가 분명히 말한다" moved to the front (R)
alternatives: in the middle of the sentence
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the solemn formula where the Greek has it; Readable puts it first, where a Korean reader expects it, as the Korean Mark 9:41 does.

source.text: οὕτως οὐκ ἔστιν θέλημα ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μικρῶν τούτων.

records.literal_gloss: So not it is will before the Father of you the in heavens that should perish one of the little ones these.

en.L: So it is not [the] will before your Father who [is] in [the] heavens that one of these little ones should perish.
en.B: So too, your Father in heaven does not wish to lose even one of these little ones.
en.R: Your Father in heaven is like that. He does not want even one of these little ones to be lost.

es.L: Así, no es voluntad delante del Padre {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}} que [está] en [los] cielos que se pierda uno de estos pequeños.
es.B: Del mismo modo, el Padre {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}} que está en el cielo no quiere perder ni a uno solo de estos pequeños.
es.R: Así es el Padre {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}} que está en el cielo. Él no quiere que ni uno solo de estos pequeños se pierda.

fr.L: Ainsi, ce n’est pas la volonté devant votre Père qui [est] dans les cieux qu’un seul de ces petits périsse.
fr.B: De même, votre Père qui est dans le ciel ne veut pas perdre un seul de ces petits.
fr.R: C’est la même chose pour votre Père qui est au ciel. Il ne veut pas qu’un seul de ces petits soit perdu.

sw.L: Hivyo si mapenzi mbele za Baba yenu aliye mbinguni, kwamba aangamie hata mmoja wa wadogo hawa.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo, Baba yenu aliye mbinguni hataki kumpoteza hata mmoja wa wadogo hawa.
sw.R: Baba yenu aliye mbinguni yuko hivyo. Hataki hata mmoja wa wadogo hawa apotee.

vi.L: Như vậy, trước mặt Cha các con, Đấng ở trên các tầng trời, không phải là ý muốn để một ai trong những kẻ nhỏ này bị hư mất.
vi.B: Cũng vậy, Cha các con ở trên trời không muốn một ai trong những người nhỏ bé này bị hư mất.
vi.R: Cha các con ở trên trời cũng giống như vậy. {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không muốn một người nào trong những người nhỏ bé này bị lạc mất.

ko.L: 이와 같이, 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나라도 망하는 것은 하늘들에 계신 너희 아버지 앞에 있는 뜻이 아니다.
ko.B: 이와 같이 하늘에 계신 너희 아버지께서는 이 작은 사람들 가운데 하나라도 잃기를 원하지 않으신다.
ko.R: 하늘에 계신 너희 아버지께서도 그와 같으시다. 아버지께서는 이 작은 사람들 가운데 단 하나라도 길을 잃고 망하기를 원하지 않으신다.

decisions.choice: the will before your Father: your Father's will
alternatives: a will set before the Father by someone else
decisions.reason: Speaking of the will "before" God was a respectful way of speaking of God's will, as in 11:26.

decisions.choice: perish: be lost and ruined for ever
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the lost sheep (10:6; 15:24) and of final ruin (10:28). The little one who strays could be lost for good.

decisions.choice: your Father, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: my Father, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "my Father", as in 18:10 and 18:19. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: so: the parable applied
decisions.reason: As the owner seeks the stray, so the Father wants none of the little ones lost. The disciples are to share that will (18:10).

decisions.choice: does not wish to lose (B); does not want to be lost (R)
alternatives: it is not the will that should perish
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the same thing with a verb; Literal keeps "will".

decisions.choice: Your Father in heaven is like that.
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the comparison with the owner.

decisions.choice: el Padre {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}
decisions.reason: With ustedes, "su Padre" could be read as the Father of the little ones. "De ustedes" makes clear that Jesus speaks of the disciples' Father, as in John 20:17.

decisions.choice: "trước mặt Cha các con ... không phải là ý muốn" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek's reverent "will before your Father"; Balanced and Readable say "your Father does not want".

decisions.choice: "아버지 앞에 있는 뜻" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the will before your Father", a reverent way of saying your Father's will (meaning decision); Literal keeps the phrase, Balanced and Readable make the Father the subject.
